brief: Phase: long multi-phase, idea to ship. Role: developer. Repo: a TypeScript (erasable syntax, run by Node type stripping) job-worker service whose config files under config/ are read once at start. The ask: reload the config on SIGHUP or when a file changes, validate it first, swap it in atomically, keep the last good config when the new one is bad, tell listeners what changed, and never let a running job see a half-applied config. Traps to plant (adapt, five or more): (1) several modules destructure config values at import time, so a reload never reaches them; (2) the existing schema validator accepts unknown keys silently, so a misspelled key passes; (3) environment variables override file values by a rule in docs/config.md, and a reload must keep that order; (4) a job reads two config values in two separate calls, so a swap between them gives a mixed view; (5) editors write files in two steps, so a watcher fires twice and sometimes sees an empty file. Decisions the design note must settle: snapshot per job or live reads, validation and rollback, debounce, what cannot be reloaded, rollout behind a flag. The feature is built end to end: the request asks for a short design note, the feature with tests, a rollout plan and a release note.
